source.text: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ καὶ Τιμόθεος ὁ ἀδελφὸς τοῖς ἐν Κολοσσαῖς ἁγίοις καὶ πιστοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ· χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Paul, apostle of Christ Jesus through [the] will of God, and Timothy the brother, \v 2 to the in Colossae holy [ones] and faithful brothers in Christ: grace to you and peace from God Father of us.

en.L: Paul, an apostle of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus through [the] will of God, and Timothy [our] brother, \v 2 to the holy and faithful {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} [who are] in Colossae: grace to you and peace from God our Father.
en.B: From Paul, an apostle of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus by the will of God, and from Timothy our brother, \v 2 to God's holy people in Colossae, the faithful {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Grace and peace to you from God our Father.
en.R: This letter is from Paul and from our brother Timothy. It was God's will that I, Paul, should be an apostle, sent out by {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. \v 2 We are writing to God's holy people in the town of Colossae, our faithful {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} who belong to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. May God our Father show you grace and give you peace.

es.L: Pablo, apóstol de {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} Jesús por [la] voluntad de Dios, y Timoteo [nuestro] hermano, \v 2 a los santos y fieles hermanos en {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} [que están] en Colosas: gracia a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y paz de parte de Dios nuestro Padre.
es.B: De Pablo, apóstol {{christos:de Cristo Jesús|del Mesías Jesús}} por la voluntad de Dios, y de Timoteo, nuestro hermano, \v 2 al pueblo santo de Dios en Colosas, los hermanos fieles en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}. Gracia y paz a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} de parte de Dios nuestro Padre.
es.R: Esta carta es de Pablo y de nuestro hermano Timoteo. Dios quiso que yo, Pablo, fuera apóstol, enviado por {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}. \v 2 Escribimos al pueblo santo de Dios en la ciudad de Colosas, nuestros hermanos fieles que pertenecen {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}. Que Dios nuestro Padre {{plural_you:les|os}} dé gracia y paz.

fr.L: Paul, apôtre du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus par la volonté de Dieu, et Timothée [notre] frère, \v 2 aux saints et fidèles {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} [qui sont] à Colosses : grâce à vous et paix de la part de Dieu notre Père.
fr.B: De la part de Paul, apôtre du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus par la volonté de Dieu, et de Timothée notre frère, \v 2 au peuple saint de Dieu qui est à Colosses, les {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} fidèles {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}. Grâce et paix à vous de la part de Dieu notre Père.
fr.R: Cette lettre vient de Paul et de notre frère Timothée. Dieu a voulu que moi, Paul, je sois apôtre, envoyé par le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus. \v 2 Nous écrivons au peuple saint de Dieu dans la ville de Colosses, à nos {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} fidèles qui appartiennent au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. Que Dieu notre Père vous donne la grâce et la paix.

sw.L: Paulo, mtume wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu kwa mapenzi ya Mungu, na Timotheo ndugu [yetu], \v 2 kwa watakatifu na ndugu waaminifu katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} [walioko] Kolosai: neema kwenu na amani kutoka kwa Mungu Baba yetu.
sw.B: Kutoka kwa Paulo, mtume wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu kwa mapenzi ya Mungu, na kutoka kwa Timotheo ndugu yetu, \v 2 kwa watakatifu wa Mungu walioko Kolosai, ndugu waaminifu katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Neema na amani ziwe nanyi kutoka kwa Mungu Baba yetu.
sw.R: Barua hii inatoka kwa Paulo na kwa ndugu yetu Timotheo. Mungu alitaka mimi, Paulo, niwe mtume niliyetumwa na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. \v 2 Tunawaandikia watu wa Mungu walio watakatifu katika mji wa Kolosai, ndugu zetu waaminifu walio wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Mungu Baba yetu awaonyeshe neema na kuwapa amani.

decisions.choice: apostle: a messenger sent out with the authority of the one who sends him
alternatives: a missionary or church worker in general
decisions.reason: ἀπόστολος means one who is sent. Paul uses it for those commissioned by the risen Christ to speak for him, and counts himself among them (1 Corinthians 15:7-9; Galatians 1:1). He holds the role "through the will of God", not by any human choice.

decisions.choice: one group, described two ways: God's holy people, who are also faithful brothers and sisters in Christ
alternatives: two groups: the holy ones, and the faithful brothers
decisions.reason: One article, τοῖς, covers the whole phrase, so ἁγίοις and ἀδελφοῖς describe the same people. ἁγίοις can be an adjective with ἀδελφοῖς ("holy and faithful brothers") or Paul's usual word for believers as God's holy people (Philippians 1:1); either way the whole church is meant. ἀδελφοῖς is masculine plural, the ordinary way to address a group of men and women together.

decisions.choice: faithful: trustworthy and loyal to Christ
decisions.reason: πιστοῖς can mean "believing" or "faithful". Paul is not singling out the loyal few; he greets the whole church as people who are true to Christ, and the letter goes on to urge them to stay that way against teaching that would draw them off (2:4-8).

decisions.choice: Colossae: a small town in the Lycus valley, in the Roman province of Asia
decisions.reason: The letter names the two neighboring towns, Laodicea and Hierapolis (2:1; 4:13). Paul had not visited the church himself (2:1); the gospel had reached the town through Epaphras (1:7).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "from God our Father", without "and the Lord Jesus Christ"
alternatives: "from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "and the Lord Jesus Christ", the wording of Paul's other greetings (Philippians 1:2). Important early manuscripts have the shorter text, and a copyist is more likely to have added the familiar words than to have dropped them. The meaning of the greeting is not changed.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus; in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is written to the whole church, women and men (4:15 greets Nympha and the church in her house). "Brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: God's holy people
decisions.reason: As in Philippians 1:1: in current English "saints" suggests unusually good people, not a whole congregation.

decisions.choice: It was God's will that I, Paul, should be an apostle, sent out by {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus
alternatives: an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God
decisions.reason: Readable says what an apostle is and turns the opening of the letter into ordinary sentences, as Philippians 1:1 does.

decisions.choice: May God our Father show you grace and give you peace
alternatives: Grace to you and peace from God our Father
decisions.reason: Readable makes the greeting a prayer, as Philippians 1:2 does.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As in Philippians 4:1, Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so adding "y hermanas" would add words the Greek does not have. The whole church is meant (4:15 greets Nympha). A reviewer may prefer to make the women explicit.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Paul writes to the church in the plural throughout the letter. Every plural "you" and every verb addressed to the readers is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain), as in Philippians.

decisions.choice: {{christos:de Cristo Jesús|del Mesías Jesús}}; {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}
decisions.reason: With the article, "de" and "a" contract ("del Mesías", "al Mesías"), so the preposition goes inside the span. Literal keeps "de {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} Jesús" without the article, as the English Literal does.

decisions.choice: "du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}", "le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}", "au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}"; "{{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}" for "in Christ" (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: French cannot say "en Messie": the title needs an article, and "en" does not take one. So the span for Paul's phrase "in Christ" covers the preposition, with the familiar French "en Christ" as the default and "dans le Messie" as the alternative. Elsewhere the article stays outside the span ("du Christ" / "du Messie", "au Christ" / "au Messie"), since both read naturally; Literal adds it without brackets, as French needs it with the preposition. "Jesus Christ" is "Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}" at Balanced and Readable, as in Hebrews.

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} for the readers (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in English, the church is addressed as men and women together; "frères" stays available as the traditional form. Agreeing words follow the noun and need no span ("les frères et sœurs fidèles" / "les frères fidèles").

decisions.choice: ndugu, no gender span
decisions.reason: Swahili "ndugu" means a brother or sister, a relative or a fellow believer, so it already includes the women of the church, and a male-only alternative would change the meaning. The same holds for "kila mtu" (every person) in verse 28: Swahili has no gender spans in this chapter.

decisions.choice: watakatifu wa Mungu (B); watu wa Mungu walio watakatifu (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "watakatifu" (holy ones). Balanced adds "wa Mungu" so that the word names God's people rather than unusually good people; Readable says it in full, as the English Balanced and Readable say "God's holy people".

source.text: Εὐχαριστοῦμεν τῷ θεῷ πατρὶ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν προσευχόμενοι, ἀκούσαντες τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην ἣν ἔχετε εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἁγίους διὰ τὴν ἐλπίδα τὴν ἀποκειμένην ὑμῖν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, ἣν προηκούσατε ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τῆς ἀληθείας τοῦ εὐαγγελίου τοῦ παρόντος εἰς ὑμᾶς, καθὼς καὶ ἐν παντὶ τῷ κόσμῳ ἐστὶν καρποφορούμενον καὶ αὐξανόμενον καθὼς καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν, ἀφ’ ἧς ἡμέρας ἠκούσατε καὶ ἐπέγνωτε τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ· καθὼς ἐμάθετε ἀπὸ Ἐπαφρᾶ τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ συνδούλου ἡμῶν, ὅς ἐστιν πιστὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν διάκονος τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁ καὶ δηλώσας ἡμῖν τὴν ὑμῶν ἀγάπην ἐν πνεύματι.

records.literal_gloss: We give thanks to the God Father of the Lord of us Jesus Christ always concerning you praying, \v 4 having heard of the faith of you in Christ Jesus and the love which you have toward all the holy [ones] \v 5 because of the hope the [one] being laid up for you in the heavens, which you heard of before in the word of the truth of the gospel \v 6 the [one] being present to you, just as also in all the world it is bearing fruit and growing, just as also among you, from which day you heard and came to know the grace of the God in truth; \v 7 just as you learned from Epaphras the beloved fellow slave of us, who is faithful on behalf of us servant of the Christ, \v 8 the [one] also having made known to us the of you love in [the] Spirit.

en.L: We give thanks to God, [the] Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, always, when praying for you, \v 4 since we heard of your faith in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus and of the love that you have for all the holy ones \v 5 because of the hope that is laid up for you in the heavens, which you heard of before in the word of the truth of the gospel \v 6 that has come to you, just as in all the world also it is bearing fruit and growing, as [it is] also among you, from the day you heard and came to know the grace of God in truth, \v 7 just as you learned [it] from Epaphras, our beloved fellow slave, who is a faithful servant of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} on our behalf, \v 8 who also made known to us your love in [the] Spirit.
en.B: Every time we pray for you, we give thanks to God, the Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, \v 4 because we have heard of your faith in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus and of the love you have for all God's holy people. \v 5 That faith and love spring from the hope kept safe for you in heaven, the hope you first heard about in the message of truth, the gospel \v 6 that has reached you. All over the world this gospel is bearing fruit and growing, and it has done the same among you from the day you heard it and came to know God's grace in all its truth. \v 7 You learned it from Epaphras, our dear fellow servant, who serves {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} faithfully on our behalf. \v 8 He is also the one who told us about your love in the Spirit.
en.R: Every time we pray for you, we thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 4 We have heard about your faith in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus and the love you have for all of God's people. \v 5 Your faith and love come from what you hope for, which God is keeping safe for you in heaven. You first heard about this hope when the message of truth, the good news, \v 6 came to you. This good news is bearing fruit and growing all over the world. It has done the same among you, ever since the day you heard it and understood the truth about God's grace. \v 7 You learned it from Epaphras. He is our dear fellow servant: like us, he belongs to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. He serves {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} faithfully in our place. \v 8 It was Epaphras who told us about the love the Spirit has given you.

es.L: Damos gracias a Dios, [el] Padre de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, siempre, cuando oramos por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, \v 4 pues hemos oído de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe en {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} Jesús y del amor que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} por todos los santos \v 5 a causa de la esperanza que {{plural_you:les|os}} está guardada en los cielos, de la cual {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} antes en la palabra de la verdad del evangelio \v 6 que ha llegado a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, así como también en todo el mundo está dando fruto y creciendo, como [lo hace] también entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, desde el día en que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} y {{plural_you:conocieron|conocisteis}} la gracia de Dios en verdad, \v 7 tal como [lo] {{plural_you:aprendieron|aprendisteis}} de Epafras, nuestro amado compañero esclavo, que es fiel servidor del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} a favor nuestro, \v 8 quien también nos dio a conocer {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} amor en [el] Espíritu.
es.B: Cada vez que oramos por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, damos gracias a Dios, el Padre de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, \v 4 porque hemos oído de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}} y del amor que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} por todo el pueblo santo de Dios. \v 5 Esa fe y ese amor brotan de la esperanza que {{plural_you:les|os}} está reservada en el cielo, la esperanza de la que {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} hablar por primera vez en el mensaje de la verdad, el evangelio \v 6 que {{plural_you:les|os}} ha llegado. En todo el mundo este evangelio está dando fruto y creciendo, y lo mismo ha ocurrido entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} desde el día en que lo {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} y {{plural_you:conocieron|conocisteis}} la gracia de Dios en toda su verdad. \v 7 Lo {{plural_you:aprendieron|aprendisteis}} de Epafras, nuestro querido consiervo, que sirve fielmente {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}} en nuestro nombre. \v 8 Él es también quien nos habló del amor que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} en el Espíritu.
es.R: Cada vez que oramos por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, damos gracias a Dios, el Padre de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. \v 4 Hemos oído de la fe que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}} y del amor que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} por todo el pueblo de Dios. \v 5 {{plural_you:Su|Vuestra}} fe y {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} amor nacen de lo que {{plural_you:esperan|esperáis}}, que Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} tiene guardado en el cielo. {{plural_you:Oyeron|Oísteis}} hablar de esta esperanza por primera vez cuando el mensaje de la verdad, la buena noticia, \v 6 llegó a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Esta buena noticia está dando fruto y creciendo en todo el mundo. Lo mismo ha pasado entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} desde el día en que la {{plural_you:oyeron|oísteis}} y {{plural_you:entendieron|entendisteis}} la verdad de la gracia de Dios. \v 7 La {{plural_you:aprendieron|aprendisteis}} de Epafras. Él es nuestro querido consiervo: como nosotros, pertenece {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}. Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} sirve fielmente en nuestro lugar. \v 8 Fue Epafras quien nos habló del amor que el Espíritu {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dado.

fr.L: Nous rendons grâce à Dieu, Père de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, toujours, quand nous prions pour vous, \v 4 ayant entendu parler de votre foi {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus et de l’amour que vous avez pour tous les saints \v 5 à cause de l’espérance qui vous est réservée dans les cieux, dont vous avez entendu parler auparavant dans la parole de la vérité de l’Évangile \v 6 qui est parvenu jusqu’à vous, de même que dans le monde entier aussi il porte du fruit et grandit, comme [il le fait] aussi parmi vous, depuis le jour où vous avez entendu et connu la grâce de Dieu en vérité, \v 7 ainsi que vous [l’]avez appris d’Épaphras, notre bien-aimé compagnon d’esclavage, qui est pour nous un fidèle serviteur du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, \v 8 qui nous a aussi fait connaître votre amour dans l’Esprit.
fr.B: Chaque fois que nous prions pour vous, nous remercions Dieu, le Père de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, \v 4 car nous avons entendu parler de votre foi {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus et de l’amour que vous avez pour tout le peuple saint de Dieu. \v 5 Cette foi et cet amour jaillissent de l’espérance qui vous est réservée dans le ciel, l’espérance dont vous avez entendu parler pour la première fois dans le message de la vérité, l’Évangile \v 6 qui vous est parvenu. Dans le monde entier, cet Évangile porte du fruit et grandit, et il en va de même chez vous depuis le jour où vous l’avez entendu et où vous avez connu la grâce de Dieu dans toute sa vérité. \v 7 C’est ce que vous avez appris d’Épaphras, notre cher compagnon de service, qui sert fidèlement le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} en notre nom. \v 8 C’est lui aussi qui nous a parlé de votre amour dans l’Esprit.
fr.R: Chaque fois que nous prions pour vous, nous remercions Dieu, le Père de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. \v 4 Nous avons entendu parler de votre foi {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus et de l’amour que vous avez pour tout le peuple de Dieu. \v 5 Votre foi et votre amour viennent de ce que vous espérez, et que Dieu vous garde en sûreté dans le ciel. Vous avez entendu parler de cette espérance pour la première fois quand le message de la vérité, la bonne nouvelle, \v 6 est arrivé jusqu’à vous. Cette bonne nouvelle porte du fruit et grandit dans le monde entier. Elle a fait de même chez vous, depuis le jour où vous l’avez entendue et où vous avez compris la vérité sur la grâce de Dieu. \v 7 Vous l’avez apprise d’Épaphras. C’est notre cher compagnon de service : comme nous, il appartient au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. Il {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} sert fidèlement à notre place. \v 8 C’est Épaphras qui nous a parlé de l’amour que l’Esprit vous a donné.

sw.L: Tunamshukuru Mungu, Baba wa Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, siku zote tunapowaombea, \v 4 kwa kuwa tulisikia habari ya imani yenu katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu na upendo mlio nao kwa watakatifu wote \v 5 kwa sababu ya tumaini lililowekwa akiba kwa ajili yenu katika mbingu, ambalo mlilisikia zamani katika neno la kweli la Injili \v 6 iliyowafikia, kama vile pia katika ulimwengu wote inazaa matunda na kukua, kama [inavyofanya] pia kwenu, tangu siku mliposikia na kuijua neema ya Mungu katika kweli, \v 7 kama mlivyojifunza kwa Epafra, mtumwa mwenzetu mpendwa, aliye mtumishi mwaminifu wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kwa niaba yetu, \v 8 ambaye pia alitujulisha upendo wenu katika Roho.
sw.B: Kila tunapowaombea, tunamshukuru Mungu, Baba wa Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, \v 4 kwa sababu tumesikia habari za imani yenu katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu na upendo mlio nao kwa watakatifu wote. \v 5 Imani hiyo na upendo huo vinatokana na tumaini lililohifadhiwa kwa ajili yenu mbinguni, tumaini mlilolisikia kwanza katika ujumbe wa kweli, yaani Injili \v 6 iliyowafikia. Katika ulimwengu wote Injili hii inazaa matunda na kukua, na ndivyo ilivyofanya kwenu pia tangu siku mlipoisikia na kuijua neema ya Mungu katika kweli yake yote. \v 7 Mlijifunza Injili hiyo kwa Epafra, mtumishi mwenzetu mpendwa, anayemtumikia {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kwa uaminifu kwa niaba yetu. \v 8 Yeye ndiye aliyetueleza pia habari za upendo wenu katika Roho.
sw.R: Kila tunapowaombea, tunamshukuru Mungu, Baba wa Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. \v 4 Tumesikia habari za imani yenu katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, na upendo mlio nao kwa watu wote wa Mungu. \v 5 Imani yenu na upendo wenu vinatokana na kile mnachotumaini, ambacho Mungu anawawekea salama mbinguni. Mlisikia habari za tumaini hili kwa mara ya kwanza wakati ujumbe wa kweli, yaani Habari Njema, \v 6 ulipowafikia. Habari Njema hii inazaa matunda na kukua duniani kote. Imefanya vivyo hivyo kwenu tangu siku mlipoisikia na kuielewa kweli kuhusu neema ya Mungu. \v 7 Mliisikia kutoka kwa Epafra. Yeye ni mtumishi mwenzetu mpendwa: kama sisi, yeye ni wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Anamtumikia kwa uaminifu badala yetu. \v 8 Ni Epafra aliyetueleza habari za upendo ambao Roho amewapa.

decisions.choice: verses 3-8 are one sentence
alternatives: verse 7 begins a new sentence, as the SBLGNT's raised dot allows
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a raised dot at the end of verse 6, but verse 7 opens with καθὼς ("just as") and says where the Colossians learned the grace of God they came to know in verse 6, so it cannot stand on its own. The record keeps verses 3-8 together, as Philippians 1:3-7 does; the meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: "always" goes with giving thanks: every time they pray, they give thanks
alternatives: "always" goes with praying: we give thanks, praying for you always
decisions.reason: πάντοτε stands between the verb and the participle and could go with either. In Paul's other thanksgivings "always" goes with the thanks (1 Corinthians 1:4; 1 Thessalonians 1:2), and the sense is much the same: thanks rises whenever they pray.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "God the Father"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ here, and many read "God and Father". The SBLGNT has the two nouns side by side. All the readings say that the God they thank is the Father of the Lord Jesus Christ.

decisions.choice: the hope is the ground of their faith and love
alternatives: the hope is a further reason for Paul's thanks
decisions.reason: διὰ ("because of") stands nearer to faith and love than to "we give thanks", and Paul joins faith, love and hope elsewhere (1 Corinthians 13:13; 1 Thessalonians 1:3). They trust Christ and love his people because of what God has kept for them.

decisions.choice: hope: the thing hoped for, kept safe in heaven
alternatives: hope: the feeling or attitude of hoping
decisions.reason: A hope that is ἀποκειμένην ("laid up, stored away") is something real kept in store, like an inheritance (1 Peter 1:4). In verse 27 Paul names it: Christ in them, the hope of glory.

decisions.choice: the word of truth, which is the gospel
alternatives: the true word that belongs to the gospel
decisions.reason: The genitives explain one another: the message is "the truth", and that message is the gospel. Paul stresses that what they first heard was true before he warns them about teaching that is not (2:4, 2:8).

decisions.choice: bearing fruit and growing: perhaps an echo of God's first blessing on humankind, "be fruitful and multiply"
alternatives: a simple picture of growth, with no echo
decisions.reason: The pair may recall Genesis 1:28, where God blesses humankind to be fruitful and increase; the gospel now makes a new humanity grow across the world (compare 3:10). The words are not quoted exactly, so the echo is possible, not certain. Paul uses the same pair of the believers themselves in verse 10.

decisions.choice: in truth: they came to know God's grace as it really is
alternatives: truly, sincerely: they really did come to know it
decisions.reason: ἐν ἀληθείᾳ could describe their knowing (they truly knew it) or what they knew (grace in its truth, the true gospel). With "the word of the truth" in verse 5 and Epaphras's faithful teaching in verse 7, Paul's point is that they received the real gospel.

decisions.choice: Epaphras: a Colossian, through whom they first heard the gospel
decisions.reason: Epaphras is "one of you" (4:12) and taught them the gospel. He is now with Paul (4:12-13; Philemon 23). The name is a short form of Epaphroditus, but nothing connects him with the Epaphroditus of Philippians 2:25.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "on our behalf"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "on your behalf"; in Greek the two words differ by a single letter. With "on our behalf", Epaphras works in Colossae as Paul's representative. With "on your behalf", he serves Christ for the Colossians' good, as in 4:12-13. Reviewers should check the manuscript evidence.

decisions.choice: servant: one who serves another, here Christ
decisions.reason: διάκονος is the general word for someone who serves (in Philippians 1:1 it names a group in the church). Paul uses it of himself as servant of the gospel (verse 23) and of the church (verse 25).

decisions.choice: love that the Spirit produces
alternatives: spiritual love, as opposed to physical
decisions.reason: πνεύματι most likely means the Holy Spirit, who gives love (Galatians 5:22; Romans 15:30). This is the only place in the letter where the Spirit is named.

decisions.choice: fellow slave: one who belongs, as Paul does, to the same master, Christ
decisions.reason: συνδούλου joins "with" to the word for a slave. Paul calls himself and Timothy slaves of Christ (Philippians 1:1), people who belong wholly to him; Epaphras belongs to the same master. He uses the same word of Tychicus in 4:7, and calls Epaphras "a slave of Christ Jesus" in 4:12.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article in verse 7: "the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}".

decisions.choice: fellow servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m13) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave". Readable adds what it means: like Paul, he belongs to Christ.

decisions.choice: Every time we pray for you, we give thanks
alternatives: We give thanks ..., always praying for you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the prayer first, so that "always" is plainly about the thanks (m2).

decisions.choice: That faith and love spring from the hope (B); Your faith and love come from what you hope for (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "because of the hope" is tied to (m4).

decisions.choice: the love the Spirit has given you
decisions.reason: Readable states the sense chosen in m12.

decisions.choice: consiervo
decisions.reason: "Consiervo" in Balanced and Readable, as "fellow servant" in the English and the style guide; the meaning decision (m13) keeps that Epaphras belongs wholly to Christ, and Literal keeps "compañero esclavo". In Balanced and Readable the other word in the verse is a verb ("sirve"), so the two do not clash.

decisions.choice: servidor (διάκονος)
decisions.reason: "Servidor" is the plain word for one who serves (m11), and keeps διάκονος apart from "esclavo" (συνδούλου) in the same verse. "Siervo" is avoided for it because it would blur the two; "ministro" suggests a church office. The same word is used in verses 23 and 25.

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level (for the whole letter)
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: Colossians is a letter: Paul speaks to the readers about what they heard, learned and received, and French uses the passé composé for that ("vous avez entendu", "Dieu nous a délivrés"). The letter has no narrative passage that would call for the passé simple.

decisions.choice: l’Évangile (L, B); la bonne nouvelle (R) (for the whole letter)
alternatives: la bonne nouvelle at every level
decisions.reason: As in English, Readable says "good news" because "Évangile" is church language. The capital marks the message itself and keeps it apart from a book of the Gospels being meant.

decisions.choice: mtumwa mwenzetu (L), mtumishi mwenzetu (B, R); mtumishi (διάκονος)
decisions.reason: "Mtumwa" (slave) in συνδούλου in Literal; Balanced and Readable have "mtumishi mwenzetu", as the English has "fellow servant" (style guide, m13). "Mtumishi" (one who serves) is kept for διάκονος here and in verses 23 and 25, so the two Greek words stay apart. In Balanced and Readable the other word is a verb ("anamtumikia"), so the two still do not clash.

decisions.choice: Anamtumikia: no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English Readable has "serves {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}". Swahili puts the object inside the verb (a-na-m-tumikia), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so there is no span. The setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives (yeye, wake, yake), so the Swahili has fewer spans than the English throughout the letter.

source.text: Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἡμεῖς, ἀφ’ ἧς ἡμέρας ἠκούσαμεν, οὐ παυόμεθα ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν προσευχόμενοι καὶ αἰτούμενοι ἵνα πληρωθῆτε τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ καὶ συνέσει πνευματικῇ, περιπατῆσαι ἀξίως τοῦ κυρίου εἰς πᾶσαν ἀρεσκείαν ἐν παντὶ ἔργῳ ἀγαθῷ καρποφοροῦντες καὶ αὐξανόμενοι τῇ ἐπιγνώσει τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει δυναμούμενοι κατὰ τὸ κράτος τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ εἰς πᾶσαν ὑπομονὴν καὶ μακροθυμίαν μετὰ χαρᾶς, εὐχαριστοῦντες τῷ πατρὶ τῷ ἱκανώσαντι ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν μερίδα τοῦ κλήρου τῶν ἁγίων ἐν τῷ φωτί, ὃς ἐρρύσατο ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ σκότους καὶ μετέστησεν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς ἀγάπης αὐτοῦ, ἐν ᾧ ἔχομεν τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν, τὴν ἄφεσιν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν·

records.literal_gloss: Because of this also we, from which day we heard, do not cease on behalf of you praying and asking that you may be filled [with] the knowledge of the will of him in all wisdom and understanding spiritual, \v 10 to walk worthily of the Lord unto all pleasing, in every work good bearing fruit and growing in the knowledge of the God, \v 11 with all power being empowered according to the might of the glory of him unto all endurance and patience with joy, \v 12 giving thanks to the Father, the [one] having qualified you for the share of the lot of the holy [ones] in the light, \v 13 who rescued us out of the authority of the darkness and transferred [us] into the kingdom of the Son of the love of him, \v 14 in whom we have the redemption, the forgiveness of the sins.

en.L: Because of this we also, from the day we heard, do not stop praying for you and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding, \v 10 to walk worthily of the Lord, to please [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] in every way, bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God, \v 11 being made strong with all power according to the might of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory for all endurance and patience with joy, \v 12 giving thanks to the Father, who qualified you for [your] share of the inheritance of the holy ones in the light, \v 13 who rescued us from the authority of darkness and transferred [us] into the kingdom of the Son of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} love, \v 14 in whom we have the redemption, the forgiveness of sins.
en.B: That is why, from the day we heard about you, we have not stopped praying for you. We ask God to fill you with the knowledge of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will, with all the wisdom and understanding the Spirit gives, \v 10 so that you may live in a way worthy of the Lord and please {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in every way, bearing fruit in every kind of good work and growing in the knowledge of God. \v 11 We ask that you be made strong with all power by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious might, so that you may endure everything with patience and joy, \v 12 and give thanks to the Father, who has made you fit to share in the inheritance of God's holy people in the light. \v 13 He has rescued us from the power of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of the Son {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves. \v 14 In {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} we have redemption, which is the forgiveness of our sins.
en.R: So ever since we heard about you, we have not stopped praying for you. We ask God to help you understand fully what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants, and to give you all the wisdom and understanding that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit gives. \v 10 Then you will live in a way that honors the Lord and pleases {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in everything. Your lives will bear fruit as you do every kind of good work, and you will keep growing in knowing God. \v 11 We pray that God will make you strong with all the power of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, so that you can keep going and stay patient whatever happens, and do it with joy. \v 12 And you will thank the Father, who has made you fit to receive your share of everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has kept for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people in the kingdom of light. \v 13 God has rescued us from the power of darkness and has brought us into the kingdom of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son, whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loves. \v 14 Through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son we have been set free: our sins are forgiven.

es.L: Por esto también nosotros, desde el día en que [lo] oímos, no dejamos de orar por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y de pedir que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} llenos del conocimiento de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voluntad en toda sabiduría y entendimiento espiritual, \v 10 para andar de manera digna del Señor, para agradar[{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] en todo, dando fruto en toda buena obra y creciendo en el conocimiento de Dios, \v 11 siendo fortalecidos con todo poder conforme a la potencia de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria para toda perseverancia y paciencia con gozo, \v 12 dando gracias al Padre, que {{plural_you:los|os}} capacitó para la parte de la herencia de los santos en la luz, \v 13 el cual nos rescató de la autoridad de la oscuridad y [nos] trasladó al reino del Hijo de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} amor, \v 14 en quien tenemos la redención, el perdón de los pecados.
es.B: Por eso, desde el día en que oímos hablar de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, no hemos dejado de orar por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Pedimos a Dios que {{plural_you:los|os}} llene del conocimiento de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} voluntad, con toda la sabiduría y el entendimiento que da el Espíritu, \v 10 para que {{plural_you:vivan|viváis}} de una manera digna del Señor y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} {{plural_you:agraden|agradéis}} en todo, dando fruto en toda clase de buenas obras y creciendo en el conocimiento de Dios. \v 11 Pedimos que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} fortalecidos con todo poder por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} glorioso poderío, para que {{plural_you:puedan|podáis}} soportarlo todo con paciencia y gozo, \v 12 y {{plural_you:den|deis}} gracias al Padre, que {{plural_you:los|os}} ha hecho aptos para participar de la herencia del pueblo santo de Dios en la luz. \v 13 Él nos ha rescatado del poder de la oscuridad y nos ha trasladado al reino del Hijo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ama. \v 14 En {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} tenemos la redención, que es el perdón de nuestros pecados.
es.R: Por eso, desde que oímos hablar de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, no hemos dejado de orar por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Pedimos a Dios que {{plural_you:los|os}} ayude a entender bien lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quiere, y que {{plural_you:les|os}} dé toda la sabiduría y el entendimiento que da {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Espíritu. \v 10 Así {{plural_you:vivirán|viviréis}} de una manera que honre al Señor y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} agrade en todo. {{plural_you:Sus|Vuestras}} vidas darán fruto cuando {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} toda clase de buenas obras, y {{plural_you:seguirán|seguiréis}} creciendo en el conocimiento de Dios. \v 11 Oramos para que Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} haga fuertes con todo el poder de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} gloria, para que {{plural_you:puedan|podáis}} seguir adelante y tener paciencia pase lo que pase, y lo {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} con alegría. \v 12 Y {{plural_you:darán|daréis}} gracias al Padre, que {{plural_you:los|os}} ha hecho aptos para recibir {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} parte de todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha guardado para {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo santo en el reino de la luz. \v 13 Dios nos ha rescatado del poder de la oscuridad y nos ha llevado al reino de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo, a quien {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ama. \v 14 Por medio de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo hemos sido liberados: nuestros pecados están perdonados.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi nous aussi, depuis le jour où nous [l’]avons appris, nous ne cessons pas de prier pour vous et de demander que vous soyez remplis de la connaissance de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} volonté en toute sagesse et intelligence spirituelle, \v 10 pour marcher d’une manière digne du Seigneur, pour [{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}] plaire en toutes choses, portant du fruit en toute œuvre bonne et grandissant dans la connaissance de Dieu, \v 11 étant fortifiés en toute puissance selon la force de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire pour toute endurance et patience avec joie, \v 12 rendant grâce au Père, qui vous a rendus capables d’avoir part à l’héritage des saints dans la lumière, \v 13 qui nous a délivrés de l’autorité des ténèbres et [nous] a transférés dans le royaume du Fils de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} amour, \v 14 en qui nous avons la rédemption, le pardon des péchés.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi, depuis le jour où nous avons entendu parler de vous, nous n’avons pas cessé de prier pour vous. Nous demandons à Dieu de vous remplir de la connaissance de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} volonté, avec toute la sagesse et l’intelligence que donne l’Esprit, \v 10 afin que vous viviez d’une manière digne du Seigneur et que vous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} plaisiez en tout, en portant du fruit dans toutes sortes d’œuvres bonnes et en grandissant dans la connaissance de Dieu. \v 11 Nous demandons que vous soyez fortifiés en toute puissance par {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} force glorieuse, afin que vous puissiez tout endurer avec patience et avec joie, \v 12 et que vous remerciiez le Père, qui vous a rendus capables d’avoir part à l’héritage du peuple saint de Dieu dans la lumière. \v 13 Il nous a délivrés du pouvoir des ténèbres et nous a fait passer dans le royaume du Fils qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aime. \v 14 En {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} nous avons la rédemption, c’est-à-dire le pardon de nos péchés.
fr.R: Aussi, depuis que nous avons entendu parler de vous, nous n’avons pas cessé de prier pour vous. Nous demandons à Dieu de vous aider à bien comprendre ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} veut, et de vous donner toute la sagesse et l’intelligence que donne {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Esprit. \v 10 Alors vous vivrez d’une manière qui honore le Seigneur et qui {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} plaît en tout. Votre vie portera du fruit, quand vous ferez toutes sortes de bonnes actions, et vous continuerez à grandir dans la connaissance de Dieu. \v 11 Nous prions pour que Dieu vous rende forts avec toute la puissance de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} gloire. Ainsi, vous pourrez tenir bon et rester patients quoi qu’il arrive, et le faire avec joie. \v 12 Et vous remercierez le Père. Il vous a rendus capables de recevoir votre part de tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} garde pour {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple saint dans le royaume de la lumière. \v 13 Dieu nous a délivrés du pouvoir des ténèbres, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous a fait entrer dans le royaume de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aime. \v 14 Par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils, nous avons été libérés : nos péchés sont pardonnés.

sw.L: Kwa sababu hii sisi pia, tangu siku ile tuliyosikia, hatukomi kusali kwa ajili yenu na kuomba ili mjae ujuzi wa mapenzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} katika hekima yote na utambuzi wa kiroho, \v 10 ili mwenende kwa namna inayomstahili Bwana, kwa kumpendeza katika kila jambo, mkizaa matunda katika kila kazi njema na kukua katika ujuzi wa Mungu, \v 11 mkitiwa nguvu kwa nguvu zote kulingana na uweza wa utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, kwa ajili ya ustahimilivu wote na subira pamoja na furaha, \v 12 mkimshukuru Baba, aliyewafanya mfae kwa ajili ya fungu la urithi wa watakatifu katika nuru, \v 13 ambaye alituokoa kutoka katika mamlaka ya giza na akatuhamishia katika ufalme wa Mwana wa upendo {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, \v 14 ambaye ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} tuna ukombozi, msamaha wa dhambi.
sw.B: Ndiyo sababu, tangu siku tuliposikia habari zenu, hatujaacha kusali kwa ajili yenu. Tunamwomba Mungu awajaze ujuzi wa mapenzi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, pamoja na hekima yote na ufahamu unaotoka kwa Roho, \v 10 ili mpate kuishi maisha yanayomstahili Bwana na kumpendeza katika kila jambo, mkizaa matunda katika kila aina ya kazi njema na kukua katika kumjua Mungu. \v 11 Tunaomba mtiwe nguvu kwa uweza wote kwa nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} tukufu, ili mweze kustahimili kila kitu kwa subira na furaha, \v 12 na kumshukuru Baba, aliyewafanya mfae kushiriki urithi wa watakatifu wa Mungu katika nuru. \v 13 Yeye ametuokoa kutoka katika nguvu za giza, akatuleta katika ufalme wa Mwana anayempenda. \v 14 Ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} tuna ukombozi, yaani msamaha wa dhambi zetu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo tangu siku tuliposikia habari zenu, hatujaacha kuwaombea. Tunamwomba Mungu awasaidie kuelewa kikamilifu anachotaka, na kuwapa hekima yote na ufahamu ambao Roho {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} hutoa. \v 10 Hapo mtaishi maisha yanayomheshimu Bwana na kumpendeza katika kila jambo. Maisha yenu yatazaa matunda mnapofanya kila aina ya kazi njema, nanyi mtaendelea kukua katika kumjua Mungu. \v 11 Tunaomba Mungu awape nguvu kwa uweza wote wa utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, ili muweze kuendelea na kuwa na subira lolote litakalotokea, na kufanya hivyo kwa furaha. \v 12 Nanyi mtamshukuru Baba, aliyewafanya mfae kupokea fungu lenu la yote aliyowawekea watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walio watakatifu katika ufalme wa nuru. \v 13 Mungu ametuokoa kutoka katika nguvu za giza, akatuleta katika ufalme wa Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} anayempenda. \v 14 Kupitia Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} tumepata ukombozi: dhambi zetu zimesamehewa.

decisions.choice: because of this: because of the faith, love and hope they have heard about (verses 4-8)
decisions.reason: Διὰ τοῦτο looks back to the report Epaphras brought. "From the day we heard" echoes "from the day you heard" in verse 6: since the day the gospel reached Colossae, and since the day the news of it reached Paul, prayer has not stopped.

decisions.choice: knowledge: a real grasp of God's will that shapes how one lives
decisions.reason: ἐπίγνωσις is a strengthened word for knowing, used for knowledge that grasps its object (Philippians 1:9). Here it is knowledge of God's will, and verse 10 says at once what it is for: a life that pleases the Lord. Knowledge and wisdom come up again and again in the letter (2:2-3; 3:10).

decisions.choice: spiritual: given by the Spirit
alternatives: spiritual as opposed to practical or worldly
decisions.reason: πνευματικῇ qualifies both wisdom and understanding. For Paul what is "spiritual" comes from God's Spirit (1 Corinthians 2:12-14), in contrast to wisdom that is merely human (2:8, 2:23).

decisions.choice: to walk: the purpose of being filled with knowledge is a life that pleases the Lord
alternatives: a second request alongside the first
decisions.reason: The infinitive περιπατῆσαι gives the purpose or result of the prayer in verse 9. "Walk" is a common biblical picture for the way a person lives (Philippians 3:17).

decisions.choice: four participles describe the worthy life: bearing fruit, growing, being strengthened, giving thanks
alternatives: "giving thanks" is Paul's own thanks, not part of his prayer for them
decisions.reason: Each participle is plural and agrees with "you", so all four describe the Colossians' life. Even "giving thanks" in verse 12 is part of what Paul prays for them, not a new thanksgiving of his own.

decisions.choice: growing in the knowledge of God
alternatives: growing by the knowledge of God
decisions.reason: The dative ἐπιγνώσει, without a preposition, can say in what they grow or by what. The two belong together: they grow in knowing God, and knowing God makes them grow. The sense "in" matches verse 9, where knowledge is what they are filled with.

decisions.choice: the might of his glory: his glorious power
alternatives: the might shown in his glory
decisions.reason: δόξης describes κράτος. God's glory is the shining greatness of who he is, and his might comes from it.

decisions.choice: "with joy" goes with endurance and patience
alternatives: "with joy" goes with giving thanks: "joyfully giving thanks"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a comma after χαρᾶς, so joy marks the endurance: they bear hard things gladly. Without that comma the words could open verse 12, "with joy giving thanks". Both fit Paul (Philippians 4:4-6).

decisions.choice: a share of the inheritance: the picture of Israel's land given by lot, now applied to God's holy people
decisions.reason: μερίδα ("share") and κλήρου ("lot, portion") belong to the Old Testament language of land divided by lot among Israel's tribes (Joshua 14:1-5). Deuteronomy 10:9 uses the two together of the Levites, whose share was the Lord himself. God has given the Colossians, who were not Israelites, a full share in what he promised his people.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "qualified you"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "us", which matches "rescued us" in verse 13. The SBLGNT reads "you", and it is easier to see why a copyist would change "you" to "us" than the reverse. Either way the Colossians are included.

decisions.choice: "in the light" goes with the inheritance: the holy people's share is in God's realm of light
alternatives: the holy ones who live in the light
decisions.reason: Light is set against "the authority of darkness" in verse 13: two realms with two rulers. In Acts 26:18 Paul is sent to turn people "from darkness to light" so that they may receive a share among those made holy.

decisions.choice: the authority of darkness: the rule of evil that once held them
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in Luke 22:53 for the hour of Jesus' arrest. Darkness is pictured as a power with its own rule, like the powers Christ disarmed at the cross (2:15).

decisions.choice: transferred: moved from one realm to another
decisions.reason: μεθίστημι means to move someone from one place or position to another (Acts 13:22 uses it of God removing Saul as king). God has already taken believers out of the dark realm and set them in the Son's kingdom: both verbs tell of something done.

decisions.choice: the Son of his love: his beloved Son
alternatives: the Son who brings his love
decisions.reason: In biblical Greek a noun in the genitive often works like an adjective. God calls Jesus his beloved Son at his baptism (Mark 1:11).

decisions.choice: redemption: release, as of a captive or slave, here explained as the forgiveness of sins
alternatives: the payment of a ransom price
decisions.reason: ἀπολύτρωσιν means setting free, as a slave or captive was set free. Paul explains it at once: the release is the forgiveness of sins (compare Ephesians 1:7). The idea of a price paid is in the background (1 Corinthians 6:20) but is not the point here.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "through his blood"
decisions.reason: Some later manuscripts add "through his blood", taken from the matching words in Ephesians 1:7. The earliest manuscripts do not have it. Colossians speaks of his blood in verse 20.

decisions.choice: the wisdom and understanding the Spirit gives
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the wisdom comes from (m3); Literal keeps "spiritual".

decisions.choice: live
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a figure of speech for the way one lives (m4); Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: made you fit
decisions.reason: God himself has made them able to have this share. "Made fit" says so without suggesting an exam they passed.

decisions.choice: your share of everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has kept for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy people in the kingdom of light
alternatives: the share of the inheritance of the holy ones in the light
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of an inheritance and of light as a realm (m9, m11).

decisions.choice: Through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son
decisions.reason: Readable names the Son and says what "in him" means here: it is through him that we are set free.

decisions.choice: agradar[{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] (L); {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} agraden (B, R)
decisions.reason: Spanish object pronouns referring to God take the deity_pronoun span like free pronouns. Where the pronoun is joined to an infinitive, the span sits on the ending only ("agradar[le]"). Literal brackets it because the Greek has the noun "pleasing" and no pronoun.

decisions.choice: hemos sido liberados
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "redención". Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does: release, here the forgiveness of sins (m15).

decisions.choice: every French pronoun for God or Christ carries the deity_pronoun span, subject "il" included (for the whole letter)
alternatives: subject pronouns without the span, as in Spanish
decisions.reason: As in Hebrews: French must write the subject pronoun, so "il" for God or Christ carries the span wherever the English "he" does, and also where French needs a pronoun the English lacks ("qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aime", "Il {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} sert" in 1:7). The forms are il, lui, le, l’, son, sa, ses, lui-même. A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital.

decisions.choice: rendus capables
decisions.reason: "Dignes" would suggest that the readers had earned their share. The verb means that God himself made them able to have it, as the English "made fit" says.

decisions.choice: ujuzi (ἐπίγνωσιν); kumjua Mungu (B, R in verse 10)
decisions.reason: "Ujuzi" is knowing that comes from acquaintance and experience, which fits a grasp of God's will that shapes a life (m2). "Maarifa" and "elimu" lean towards information and schooling. In verse 10 Balanced and Readable turn the noun into the verb ("kukua katika kumjua Mungu"), which is the more natural Swahili.

decisions.choice: tumepata ukombozi
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "we have been set free". Swahili "ukombozi" is an everyday word (it is used of national liberation), so Readable keeps it and explains it with the clause that follows.

source.text: ὅς ἐστιν εἰκὼν τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ἀοράτου, πρωτότοκος πάσης κτίσεως, ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ ἐκτίσθη τὰ πάντα ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, τὰ ὁρατὰ καὶ τὰ ἀόρατα, εἴτε θρόνοι εἴτε κυριότητες εἴτε ἀρχαὶ εἴτε ἐξουσίαι· τὰ πάντα δι’ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἰς αὐτὸν ἔκτισται·

records.literal_gloss: who is image of the God the invisible, firstborn of all creation, \v 16 because in him were created the all things in the heavens and on the earth, the visible and the invisible, whether thrones or lordships or rulers or authorities; the all things through him and for him have been created;

en.L: He is [the] image of the invisible God, [the] firstborn of all creation, \v 16 because in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all things were created, in the heavens and on the earth, the visible and the invisible, whether thrones or lordships or rulers or authorities; all things have been created through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The Son is the image of the unseen God, the firstborn who stands above all creation. \v 16 For in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} everything in heaven and on earth was created, the seen and the unseen, whether thrones or dominions, rulers or authorities. Everything has been created through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: No one can see God, but the Son shows us what God is like. The Son is the firstborn: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has first place over everything God has made. \v 16 For it was by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that God made everything, in heaven and on earth, the things we can see and the things we cannot. That includes every power that rules: thrones and lords, rulers and authorities, in the spiritual world as well as in this one. God made everything through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Él es [la] imagen del Dios invisible, [el] primogénito de toda creación, \v 16 porque en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} fueron creadas todas las cosas, en los cielos y sobre la tierra, las visibles y las invisibles, sean tronos, sean señoríos, sean principados, sean autoridades; todas las cosas han sido creadas por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: El Hijo es la imagen del Dios que no se ve, el primogénito que está por encima de toda la creación. \v 16 Porque en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} fue creado todo lo que hay en el cielo y en la tierra, lo visible y lo invisible, ya sean tronos o dominios, gobernantes o autoridades. Todo ha sido creado por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Nadie puede ver a Dios, pero el Hijo nos muestra cómo es Dios. El Hijo es el primogénito: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} tiene el primer lugar sobre todo lo que Dios ha hecho. \v 16 Porque por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hizo Dios todas las cosas, en el cielo y en la tierra, las que podemos ver y las que no podemos ver. Eso incluye todo poder que gobierna: tronos y señores, gobernantes y autoridades, tanto en el mundo espiritual como en este. Dios lo hizo todo por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Il est [l’]image du Dieu invisible, [le] premier-né de toute création, \v 16 car en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont été créées toutes choses, dans les cieux et sur la terre, les visibles et les invisibles, soit trônes, soit seigneuries, soit principautés, soit autorités ; toutes choses ont été créées par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Le Fils est l’image du Dieu qu’on ne voit pas, le premier-né qui est au-dessus de toute la création. \v 16 Car c’est en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que tout a été créé, dans le ciel et sur la terre, le visible et l’invisible, trônes ou souverainetés, principautés ou autorités. Tout a été créé par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Personne ne peut voir Dieu, mais le Fils nous montre à quoi Dieu ressemble. Le Fils est le premier-né : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a la première place, au-dessus de tout ce que Dieu a fait. \v 16 Car c’est par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que Dieu a tout fait, dans le ciel et sur la terre, ce que nous pouvons voir et ce que nous ne pouvons pas voir. Cela comprend toutes les puissances qui dominent : trônes et seigneurs, chefs et autorités, dans le monde spirituel comme dans le nôtre. Dieu a tout fait par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Yeye ni sura ya Mungu asiyeonekana, mzaliwa wa kwanza wa uumbaji wote, \v 16 kwa sababu ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} viliumbwa vitu vyote, vilivyo katika mbingu na juu ya nchi, vinavyoonekana na visivyoonekana, viwe viti vya enzi au ubwana au watawala au mamlaka; vitu vyote vimeumbwa kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} na kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Mwana ni sura ya Mungu asiyeonekana, mzaliwa wa kwanza aliye juu ya viumbe vyote. \v 16 Kwa maana ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} vitu vyote viliumbwa, vya mbinguni na vya duniani, vinavyoonekana na visivyoonekana, viwe viti vya enzi au tawala, watawala au mamlaka. Vyote vimeumbwa kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} na kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Hakuna mtu awezaye kumwona Mungu, lakini Mwana anatuonyesha jinsi Mungu alivyo. Mwana ni mzaliwa wa kwanza: {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ana nafasi ya kwanza juu ya kila kitu ambacho Mungu ameumba. \v 16 Kwa maana Mungu aliumba kila kitu kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, mbinguni na duniani, vitu tunavyoweza kuona na vile tusivyoweza kuona. Hilo linajumuisha kila nguvu inayotawala: viti vya enzi na mabwana, watawala na wenye mamlaka, katika ulimwengu wa roho na katika ulimwengu huu pia. Mungu aliumba kila kitu kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} na kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

decisions.choice: who: the Son of God's love (verse 13)
decisions.reason: ὅς continues from verses 13-14, so the subject of verses 15-20 is the Son. These verses have a balanced shape, like a poem or hymn: verses 15-16 praise the Son as the one through whom all things were made, and verses 18-20 as the one through whom all things are made new. Both halves turn on the word πρωτότοκος ("firstborn").

decisions.choice: image: the Son makes the unseen God visible and known
alternatives: image: a mere likeness or copy
decisions.reason: An εἰκὼν is a likeness that shows the one it represents. God cannot be seen (John 1:18; 1 Timothy 1:17), but in the Son he is seen (2 Corinthians 4:4). The word also recalls Genesis 1:26-27, where humans are made in God's image; in Christ that image is shown in full, and believers are being renewed in it (3:10).

decisions.choice: firstborn: the one with the rank and rights of the firstborn, supreme over creation, not the first thing created
alternatives: born before creation, in time only
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament the firstborn son held first place and was heir, and God says of the king he chooses that he will set him as firstborn, high above the kings of the earth (Psalm 89:28). Verse 16 gives the reason for the title: all things were created in him, so he is not one of the created things. The genitive πάσης κτίσεως can mean "of" or "over" all creation; with this sense he stands above it.

decisions.choice: in him: God made all things in the Son and by him
alternatives: in him: within him, as in a place
decisions.reason: ἐν αὐτῷ may name Christ as the means of creation, like "through him" at the end of the verse, or as the one in whom creation has its pattern and meaning. The passive ἐκτίσθη ("were created") leaves God as the creator, acting in the Son (compare John 1:3; Hebrews 1:2).

decisions.choice: thrones, dominions, rulers, authorities: ranks of powers, especially unseen spiritual powers
decisions.reason: Jewish writings of Paul's day named orders of angelic powers, and Paul uses "rulers and authorities" of spiritual powers (2:15; Ephesians 6:12). The list follows "the invisible", so unseen powers are mainly in view, though earthly rulers are not excluded. Whatever powers the Colossians feared or honored (2:18) were made by Christ and for him.

decisions.choice: for him: Christ is the goal of creation, and creation stands as his work
decisions.reason: εἰς αὐτὸν names the purpose for which everything exists. The verb changes from ἐκτίσθη ("were created", the act) to ἔκτισται ("have been created", a perfect), so creation is seen as an act whose results last.

decisions.choice: He (L); The Son (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek continues the sentence of verses 13-14 with "who". Every level starts a new sentence here; Balanced and Readable name the Son so the reader knows who is meant.

decisions.choice: lordships (L); dominions (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the link with the word for "lord"; Balanced uses the usual English word for the realm of a lord.

decisions.choice: the firstborn who stands above all creation (B); has first place over everything God has made (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the title means here (m3), so that it is not read as "the first thing created".

decisions.choice: No one can see God, but the Son shows us what God is like
alternatives: He is the image of the invisible God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "image" means here (m2).

decisions.choice: every power that rules: thrones and lords, rulers and authorities, in the spiritual world as well as in this one
alternatives: whether thrones or dominions or rulers or authorities
decisions.reason: Readable says what the four titles are (m5).

decisions.choice: señoríos, principados (L); dominios, gobernantes (B)
decisions.reason: "Principados" is the traditional Spanish word for ἀρχαὶ and keeps its link with "principio" (verse 18), so Literal uses it, with "señoríos" for the word built on "lord". For most readers today "principado" is a small country such as Monaco, so Balanced and Readable say "gobernantes" (rulers).

decisions.choice: seigneuries (L), souverainetés (B); principautés et autorités (L, B), chefs et autorités (R); the same for "rulers and authorities" in 2:10 and 2:15
decisions.reason: "Principautés" is the established French word for this rank of unseen powers, and it keeps the link with "commencement" no better than English does, so it is used wherever Paul pairs the word with "authorities". "Seigneuries" at Literal keeps the link with "Seigneur", as the English "lordships" does. Readable says "chefs", a plain word, and explains the list.

decisions.choice: sura
decisions.reason: "Mfano" is the familiar word here, but today it mostly means an example or illustration. "Sura" is form, face and appearance, the visible likeness that shows the one it represents (m2). Readable explains it as the English Readable does. For review by a native speaker.

decisions.choice: ubwana (L); tawala (B)
decisions.reason: Literal uses "ubwana" (lordship), built on "bwana", to keep the link with the word for lord, as the English Literal does; Balanced uses "tawala" (dominions, realms of rule).

source.text: καὶ αὐτός ἐστιν πρὸ πάντων καὶ τὰ πάντα ἐν αὐτῷ συνέστηκεν, καὶ αὐτός ἐστιν ἡ κεφαλὴ τοῦ σώματος τῆς ἐκκλησίας· ὅς ἐστιν ἀρχή, πρωτότοκος ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν, ἵνα γένηται ἐν πᾶσιν αὐτὸς πρωτεύων, ὅτι ἐν αὐτῷ εὐδόκησεν πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα κατοικῆσαι καὶ δι’ αὐτοῦ ἀποκαταλλάξαι τὰ πάντα εἰς αὐτόν, εἰρηνοποιήσας διὰ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ σταυροῦ αὐτοῦ, δι’ αὐτοῦ εἴτε τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς εἴτε τὰ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς·

records.literal_gloss: and he is before all things and the all things in him hold together, \v 18 and he is the head of the body, the church; who is beginning, firstborn from the dead, so that he may become in all things himself holding first place, \v 19 because in him was pleased all the fullness to dwell \v 20 and through him to reconcile the all things to him, having made peace through the blood of the cross of him, through him, whether the things on the earth or the things in the heavens;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is before all things, and all things hold together in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \v 18 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the head of the body, the church. He is [the] beginning, [the] firstborn from the dead, so that in all things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} might come to have first place, \v 19 because in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} all the fullness was pleased to dwell \v 20 and through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to reconcile all things to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, having made peace through the blood of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cross, through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, whether the things on the earth or the things in the heavens.
en.B: He exists before all things, and all things are held together in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 18 He is also the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning, the first to be born from among the dead, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would come to hold first place in everything. \v 19 For God in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fullness was pleased to dwell in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \v 20 and through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to reconcile all things to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, making peace by the blood of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cross: all things through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, on earth and in heaven alike.
en.R: The Son existed before everything else, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} holds everything together. \v 18 He is also the head of the church, which is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} leads it and gives it life. He is where God's new creation begins, the first to rise from the dead, never to die again. So in everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has first place. \v 19 For God was pleased to live fully in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, with all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is, \v 20 and through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to bring everything back to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, everything on earth and everything in heaven. God made peace through the blood {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son poured out when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died on the cross.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es antes de todas las cosas, y todas las cosas se mantienen unidas en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, \v 18 y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es la cabeza del cuerpo, la iglesia. Él es [el] principio, [el] primogénito de entre los muertos, para que en todas las cosas {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo llegue a tener el primer lugar, \v 19 porque en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} toda la plenitud tuvo a bien habitar \v 20 y por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} reconciliar todas las cosas con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, habiendo hecho la paz mediante la sangre de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cruz, por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, ya sean las [cosas] sobre la tierra o las [cosas] en los cielos.
es.B: Él existe antes de todas las cosas, y todas las cosas se mantienen unidas en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. \v 18 Él es también la cabeza del cuerpo, la iglesia. Él es el principio, el primero en nacer de entre los muertos, para que llegue a tener el primer lugar en todo. \v 19 Porque Dios, en toda {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} plenitud, se complació en habitar en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, \v 20 y por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} reconciliar consigo todas las cosas, haciendo la paz por la sangre de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cruz: todas las cosas por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, tanto en la tierra como en el cielo.
es.R: El Hijo existía antes que todo lo demás, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mantiene todo unido. \v 18 Él es también la cabeza de la iglesia, que es {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cuerpo: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} la guía y le da vida. Con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} comienza la nueva creación de Dios; es el primero en resucitar de entre los muertos para no morir nunca más. Así, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} tiene el primer lugar en todo. \v 19 Porque Dios quiso vivir plenamente en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, con todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es, \v 20 y por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} traer todo de vuelta a {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}}, todo lo que hay en la tierra y todo lo que hay en el cielo. Dios hizo la paz por medio de la sangre que {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} Hijo derramó cuando murió en la cruz.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est avant toutes choses, et toutes choses tiennent ensemble en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, \v 18 et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est la tête du corps, l’Église. Il est [le] commencement, [le] premier-né d’entre les morts, afin qu’en toutes choses {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} devienne {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} le premier, \v 19 car en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} toute la plénitude s’est plu à habiter \v 20 et par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} à réconcilier toutes choses avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, ayant fait la paix par le sang de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} croix, par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, que ce soient les choses sur la terre ou les choses dans les cieux.
fr.B: Il existe avant toutes choses, et tout tient ensemble en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. \v 18 Il est aussi la tête du corps, qui est l’Église. Il est le commencement, le premier-né d’entre les morts, afin d’avoir en tout la première place. \v 19 Car Dieu, dans toute {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} plénitude, a trouvé bon d’habiter en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, \v 20 et par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} de réconcilier toutes choses avec {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, en faisant la paix par le sang de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} croix : toutes choses par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, sur la terre comme dans le ciel.
fr.R: Le Fils existait avant tout le reste, et c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui maintient tout ensemble. \v 18 Il est aussi la tête de l’Église, qui est {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} corps : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la conduit et lui donne la vie. C’est avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} que commence la nouvelle création de Dieu : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est le premier à se relever d’entre les morts, pour ne plus jamais mourir. Ainsi, en tout, c’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui a la première place. \v 19 Car Dieu a voulu habiter pleinement en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, avec tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est, \v 20 et par {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ramener tout à {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, tout ce qui est sur la terre et tout ce qui est dans le ciel. Dieu a fait la paix par le sang que {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} Fils a versé quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est mort sur la croix.

sw.L: Na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} yuko kabla ya vitu vyote, na vitu vyote vimeshikamana ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \v 18 na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni kichwa cha mwili, kanisa. Yeye ni mwanzo, mzaliwa wa kwanza kutoka kwa wafu, ili katika vitu vyote {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} mwenyewe apate kuwa wa kwanza, \v 19 kwa sababu ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} utimilifu wote ulipendezwa kufanya makao \v 20 na kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kuvipatanisha vitu vyote na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, baada ya kuleta amani kupitia damu ya msalaba {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, viwe vitu vya duniani au vitu vya mbinguni.
sw.B: Yeye yupo kabla ya vitu vyote, na vitu vyote vinashikamana pamoja ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \v 18 Yeye pia ni kichwa cha mwili, yaani kanisa. Yeye ndiye mwanzo, wa kwanza kuzaliwa kutoka miongoni mwa wafu, ili awe na nafasi ya kwanza katika kila kitu. \v 19 Kwa maana Mungu katika utimilifu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wote alipendezwa kukaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \v 20 na kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kuvipatanisha vitu vyote na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} mwenyewe, akileta amani kwa damu ya msalaba {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}: vitu vyote kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, vya duniani na vya mbinguni pia.
sw.R: Mwana alikuwepo kabla ya kitu kingine chochote, naye ndiye anayeshikilia kila kitu pamoja. \v 18 Yeye pia ni kichwa cha kanisa, ambalo ni mwili {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}: {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} huliongoza na kulipa uhai. Kwake uumbaji mpya wa Mungu unaanza; {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni wa kwanza kufufuka kutoka kwa wafu, wala hatakufa tena. Kwa hiyo katika kila jambo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ana nafasi ya kwanza. \v 19 Kwa maana Mungu alipendezwa kukaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kikamilifu, kwa yote alivyo, \v 20 na kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kukipatanisha kila kitu na nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kila kitu duniani na kila kitu mbinguni. Mungu alileta amani kupitia damu ambayo Mwana {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} aliimwaga alipokufa msalabani.

decisions.choice: he is before all things: before them in time and above them in rank
decisions.reason: αὐτός is emphatic: he himself. The verb is present, ἐστιν ("is", not "was"), which fits one who did not come into being with the rest (compare John 8:58).

decisions.choice: hold together: he keeps the universe in being and in order
decisions.reason: συνίστημι in the perfect means to stand together, to hold together as one whole. The one through whom all was made also keeps it from falling apart (Hebrews 1:3).

decisions.choice: head: the one who rules the body and is the source of its life
alternatives: head: the leading member within the body
decisions.reason: Here the church is Christ's body and he is its head: over it as its ruler, and the source from which it grows (2:19; Ephesians 4:15-16). In 1 Corinthians 12:21 Paul uses the picture differently, with the head as one member among others. τῆς ἐκκλησίας explains σώματος: the body is the church.

decisions.choice: beginning: the origin and first of God's new creation
alternatives: the beginning of the first creation
decisions.reason: ἀρχή can mean "beginning" or "ruler" (the plural means "rulers" in verse 16). Here it is joined to "firstborn from the dead", so it is the start of the new creation that his resurrection begins (1 Corinthians 15:20-23).

decisions.choice: firstborn from the dead: the first to rise to a life that never ends, ahead of all who will follow
decisions.reason: Others were raised before Jesus, but they died again. He is the first to rise from the dead to new, lasting life, and the first of many (1 Corinthians 15:20; Revelation 1:5). The word πρωτότοκος repeats verse 15: he is first over the old creation and first in the new.

decisions.choice: so that in everything he might come to hold first place
decisions.reason: πᾶσιν can be neuter ("in everything") or masculine ("among all"). With "all things" repeated through these verses, the neuter fits best. The verb γένηται ("might become") says that by his resurrection he came to hold the first place that verses 15-17 say was his.

decisions.choice: the fullness is God himself: God in all his fullness was pleased to dwell in the Son
alternatives: God was pleased to have all the fullness dwell in him
the fullness is a power or being of its own
decisions.reason: πλήρωμα is neuter, but the participle εἰρηνοποιήσας ("having made peace") in verse 20 is masculine, so the one who was pleased and who made peace is a person: God. 2:9 says the same thing outright: all the fullness of deity dwells in Christ bodily.

decisions.choice: dwell: settle for good, make one's home
alternatives: visit or stay for a while
decisions.reason: κατοικέω means to live in a place permanently, not as a passing guest. In 2:9 the same verb is in the present: the fullness dwells in him now.

decisions.choice: to himself: to God
alternatives: to him: to Christ, as the goal of all things (verse 16)
decisions.reason: αὐτόν could point to Christ, since verse 16 says all things were made "for him". But reconciling is God's work through Christ (2 Corinthians 5:18-19), and God is the one who was pleased in verse 19, so "to himself" is more likely.

decisions.choice: reconcile all things: bring the whole creation, on earth and in heaven, back into peace and right order under God
alternatives: every person and every power will in the end be saved
decisions.reason: Peace is made by the cross. For people, being reconciled means being brought back to God, and continuing in faith (verses 21-23). For the hostile powers, the letter speaks of their being disarmed and led in triumph (2:15). Paul does not say here how each part of creation is reconciled.

decisions.choice: the blood of his cross: Christ's violent death, given as a sacrifice
decisions.reason: Blood stands for a life given up in death, and in the Old Testament the blood of sacrifice makes atonement (Leviticus 17:11). God makes peace through Jesus' death on a Roman cross, the most shameful of deaths.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: keep the second "through him"
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts do not have the repeated "through him". If it is original, it stresses once more that all reconciliation comes through Christ. The meaning is not changed.

decisions.choice: God in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fullness was pleased (B); God was pleased to live fully in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} (R)
alternatives: all the fullness was pleased to dwell
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God as the subject (m7); Literal keeps "all the fullness".

decisions.choice: the head of the church, which is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} leads it and gives it life
alternatives: the head of the body, the church
decisions.reason: Readable says what "head" means here (m3).

decisions.choice: where God's new creation begins, the first to rise from the dead, never to die again
alternatives: the beginning, the firstborn from the dead
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two titles (m4, m5).

decisions.choice: bring everything back to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}
decisions.reason: "Reconcile" is not an everyday word for many readers; Readable says what it means, here and in verse 22.

decisions.choice: the blood {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Son poured out when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died on the cross
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the blood of his cross" refers to (m11).

decisions.choice: con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} (L); consigo (B); a {{deity_pronoun:sí mismo|Sí mismo}} (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish fuses "con" and the reflexive into one word, "consigo", which has no free pronoun to capitalise, so Balanced has no span there. Literal keeps the open "con él" of the Greek εἰς αὐτόν; Readable says "a sí mismo" (to himself, God), with the span, following m9.

decisions.choice: se mantienen unidas
decisions.reason: "Subsisten" is the traditional rendering but today means to survive or get by. "Se mantienen unidas" says what the verb means: all things hold together as one whole in him (m2).

decisions.choice: l’Église, with a capital, for the church as Christ's body (1:18, 1:24); l’église for a local congregation (4:15, 4:16) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: French marks the difference between the whole people of God and one gathering of believers with the capital. Here the church is the body whose head is Christ, so "l’Église". "Assemblée" is closer to the everyday sense of the Greek word but is not how French readers name the church.

decisions.choice: utimilifu (πλήρωμα)
decisions.reason: "Utimilifu" is fullness, the state of being full and complete; "ukamilifu" leans towards perfection or flawlessness. Use "utimilifu" again in 2:9. Readable says "kikamilifu" (fully), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: kupatanisha kept at Readable
decisions.reason: The English Readable replaces "reconcile" with "bring back". Swahili "kupatanisha" is an everyday word, used for making peace between people who have quarreled, so Readable keeps it here and in verse 22.

source.text: καὶ ὑμᾶς ποτε ὄντας ἀπηλλοτριωμένους καὶ ἐχθροὺς τῇ διανοίᾳ ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις τοῖς πονηροῖς νυνὶ δὲ ἀποκατηλλάγητε ἐν τῷ σώματι τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ διὰ τοῦ θανάτου παραστῆσαι ὑμᾶς ἁγίους καὶ ἀμώμους καὶ ἀνεγκλήτους κατενώπιον αὐτοῦ, εἴ γε ἐπιμένετε τῇ πίστει τεθεμελιωμένοι καὶ ἑδραῖοι καὶ μὴ μετακινούμενοι ἀπὸ τῆς ἐλπίδος τοῦ εὐαγγελίου οὗ ἠκούσατε, τοῦ κηρυχθέντος ἐν πάσῃ κτίσει τῇ ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανόν, οὗ ἐγενόμην ἐγὼ Παῦλος διάκονος.
